The hybrid turbine models were created using Autodesk Inventor Professional 2023 software.
The hybrid turbines had a height of 0.8 m and an outer diameter of 1.23 m.
The Magnus rotor had a diameter of 120 mm.
The computational domain had dimensions of 2.4 m, 6.0 m, and 3.0 m in the normal, streamwise, and spanwise directions, respectively.
The 3-blade turbine had 210,613 mesh elements, while the 4-blade turbine had 247,271 elements.
The researchers used the RANS model with the k-ε approach to model the turbulent flow.
The highest pressure of 92.85 Pa was generated by the 3-blade hybrid turbine at a wind velocity of 11 m/s.
The 3-blade turbine had a lower weight of 11.317 kg compared to the 4-blade turbine at 14.884 kg.
The performance difference between the 3-blade and 4-blade turbines became more pronounced at wind speeds above 7 m/s.
The Magnus rotor provides an initial rotational force to aid in the self-starting of the Savonius blades, particularly at low wind speeds.
VAWTs like the Savonius-Magnus hybrid are better suited for turbulent wind conditions and can work at lower wind speeds compared to HAWTs.
The Savonius-Magnus hybrid design can be a suitable alternative for renewable energy generation in remote or distributed applications.
The Magnus effect produces a lift force on a rotating cylinder or sphere due to the difference in air pressure on the two sides.
The smooth surface of the Magnus rotor produces less turbulence and drag compared to a stationary cylinder.
Increasing the number of blades on the Savonius turbine can enhance the wind-catching area, but too many blades can disrupt the airflow and lead to a decrease in power.
